questions.stem: What happens to the ciliary muscles and suspensory ligaments when the eye focuses on a near object?

options.text: Ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments become taut, lens becomes thin
Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments become slack, lens becomes fat and round
Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments become taut, lens becomes thin
Ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments become slack, lens becomes fat and round

questions.explanation: When focusing on a near object, the ciliary muscles contract, the suspensory ligaments become slack, and the lens becomes fat and round to refract light more strongly. This is called accommodation.
